charts.annotation: Perpetual instruments are classified in equity under HKFRS but are debt-like in substance; included in equity, they inflate book value per ordinary share.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: ShareholdersEquity here includes RMB1.5-7.1bn of perpetual capital instruments (see the Perpetual Capital chart) -- debt-like instruments that HKFRS classifies in equity. Book value per ordinary share computed straight off this line overstates what common shareholders actually own; back the perpetuals out first.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Perpetual capital instruments as a share of total equity

goldOutput.title: Gold production
goldOutput.content:
Mine-produced output is gold the group's own mines extracted and processed; total output adds gold the group smelted or traded on behalf of third parties, which carries much thinner margin.

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: revenue and the gold price move together, so neither shows whether the company is actually producing more metal. This is the volume half of the price/volume split: FY2021's dip to ~12.6t mine-produced (vs. ~19-21t in neighbouring years) was an output shortfall, not a price event. FY-only: production is reported as an annual figure in the filings, not split by half-year.

What to watch:

  • Mine-produced output trend -- the margin-accretive volume -- versus total output
  • Gap between mine-produced and total output widening (more low-margin smelting/trading mix)

perpetualCapital.title: Perpetual capital instruments
perpetualCapital.content:
Perpetual capital instruments are perpetual bonds with no fixed maturity, classified as equity under HKFRS because redemption is at the issuer's discretion -- but they carry a contractual distribution rate, which makes them debt-like in substance. Distributions paid is the cash cost of servicing them, separate from dividends paid to ordinary shareholders.

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: the balance ran RMB1.5bn (FY2020) to RMB7.1bn (FY2023) and sits inside ShareholdersEquity and outside TotalDebt -- so leverage ratios computed from either line alone understate the company's true debt-like obligations, and book value per ordinary share is overstated by the same amount.

What to watch:

  • Balance trending up (more perpetual issuance) versus down (redemption)
  • Distributions paid relative to the balance -- the effective cost of this funding

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Zhaojin Mining Industry Company Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
